newsitem.title: ITALY: Naomi Campbell signs photo-book for AIDS charity.
newsitem.headline: Naomi Campbell signs photo-book for AIDS charity.

text.p: British supermodel Naomi Campbell, her hair cropped dramatically into a neat bob, took time off the catwalk on Sunday to sign copies of her book "Naomi" and raise money for children suffering from AIDS.
Campbell, 26, wearing a chocolate brown trouser suit, a choker and pointed brown and white high-heeled shoes, said the book was a personal photographic look back at her career so far.

"I've been modelling for 10 years and it's a collection of pictures by every photographer I've ever worked with and also some by my friends," Campbell told Reuters in a brief break from signing Italian copies of the book.

"It's a big memory really. There are my school pictures in there and pictures with (South African President) Nelson Mandela," she said. "It's really like a big diary for me, a remembrance of what I've done and achieved in this business."
The hardback, which contains pictures of Campbell with other supermodels like Kate Moss and Linda Evangelista, costs 60,000 ($40) lire. The English-language version is due out in October.
Publishers Rizzoli donated cash and royalties for every copy sold to the Italian association Anlaids for children testing positive for the HIV virus which causes AIDS.

"I think that especially in Italy it's not a cause that's taken very seriously and I think it needs as much help as it can get," Campbell said. Asked how much she hoped to raise, she replied: "As much as we can."

Blonde-haired au pair Antje Kundt, 20, from Kassel in Germany battled through a crush of fans at the Rizzoli bookshop in Milan's elegant Vittorio Emmanuel shopping galleria to get her copy signed. "I just wanted to meet Naomi," she said.
Campbell's make-up artist Lamar said it had taken 20 minutes to make the blue-eyed supermodel up for the signing, while preparing her for the catwalk took about 30 to 40 minutes.
He said the process was quick and easy, adding, "She's a great canvas. I really love the shape of her eyes."
Campbell declined to comment on media speculation that she had married Italian boyfriend Luca Orlandi, saying simply: "I don't want to talk about my personal life, thank you."
Campbell, in Italy on the first day of the Milan 1997 spring/summer designer ready-to-wear fashion shows, said she had always liked Italy as a country.
She refused to be drawn when asked her opinion of Italian men, saiding she would not pick out individual aspects of the country. "I like Italy as a whole, that's it," she said.
The Milan shows run until October 6 but no major designers unveil their collections until trend-setter Miuccia Prada presents her latest line-up on Tuesday.
